prose: Patrick Collison asks what the positive AI scenario actually looks like. Curing diseases and abundance are ingredients, he says, not an equilibrium: do people work, why, what is scarce, how are resources shared? He finds fiction like the Culture novels unconvincing as a goal, and notes that earlier eras changed slowly enough for error correction, which fast AI progress may not allow. He also calls the debate on AI consciousness high-stakes, because conclusions may drive moral-worth questions.
highlights: Positive visions of AI are vague compared with risk talk
Open questions: work, scarcity, resource allocation
Fast change leaves less room for error correction
AI consciousness may matter for moral status
